title: Residency gradual enforcement timeline and edge-case catalog
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures a proposed phased approach to turning on region pinning enforcement across Private deployments, plus a catalog of edge cases and recommended mitigations. It’s intentionally operational: concrete triggers, observability signals, and rollback instructions so SRE, Platform, and Solutions can run a predictable, low-friction rollout.

Why gradual enforcement?
- Many enterprise customers have complex topology (hybrid cloud + on-prem connectors, multi-region backends, tenant-level proxies). Hard enforcement without a probe phase risks service disruption.
- We need to identify request patterns that look residency-compliant on paper but break at runtime (session handoff, model caching TTL, cross-region fallback).
- A staged timeline lets us iterate on telemetry, instrumentation, and customer comms.

Enforcement modes (definitions):
- Advisory (soft): Requests include a residency hint; system logs & emits metrics but does not block. Useful for baseline measurement.
- Soft-fail (gradual): If a request fails residency check, return a 200 with a residency-warning header and include an alternative compatible model/route. Also increment advisory counters and generate a ticket when thresholds exceeded.
- Hard-fail (strict): Reject incompatible requests with a 403/residency_violation; requires explicit customer opt-in for strict mode during the pilot.

High-level rollout timeline (proposal):
Phase 0 - Telemetry baseline (2–4 weeks)
- Mark: enable advisory mode by default for all Private instances.
- Goals: surface request-level residency labels, % of requests crossing region boundaries, cache miss rates caused by region-aware routing.
- Metrics: advisory_violation_rate, cross_region_token_rate, pinned_model_mismatch_count.
- Owner: Platform observability (Diego).

Phase 1 - Pilot soft-fail (customer opt-in, 4–6 weeks)
- Invite 5 customers across EMEA/NA/APAC to opt into soft-fail.
- For affected requests: allow response but attach X-Residency-Warning + generated ticket if repeated.
- Run daily sync between Platform and Solutions to handle operational escalations.
- Owner: Solutions (Priya) + SRE (Omar).

Phase 2 - Staged enforcement (region cohorts, 6–8 weeks)
- Move cohorts by region (e.g., start with EMEA dev clusters, then NA non-prod, then NA prod, then APAC).
- For each cohort, start in soft-fail for 1–2 weeks, then to hard-fail for a canary subset (5–10% traffic) for 3 days, then full in-region enforcement.
- Rollback window: 24 hours full rollback; instant revert to soft-fail for canary.

Phase 3 - Full enforcement + policy GA
- Hard-fail by default for new Private installs; existing installations get a migration window (90 days) to reach compliance or sign an exceptions SL.

Triggers to move phases (must pass all):
- Advisory telemetry stable: advisory_violation_rate < 0.5% for baseline across cohort for 7 days.
- Customer impact tests: fewer than 2 SEVs attributable to residency enforcement in pilot customers in 14 days.
- Observability coverage: per-request tracing enabled and sampling >= 20% for routes impacted.
- Migration tools ready: automated region-pin audit, bulk pin/replace API, and customer migration playbook published.

Edge-case catalog (examples + mitigations)
1) Cross-region session handoff (mobile client)
- Symptom: User starts a generation in EU, subsequent requests bounce to US due to LB sticky session expiry.
- Risk: data leaves region mid-session.
- Mitigation: session-level residency token; if LB would route out-of-region, route to a compatible in-region fallback model or extend stickiness TTL. Instrument session_id -> origin_region.
- Ticket example: PD-421.

2) Pinned model version drift during rollout
- Symptom: Customer pins v1.2 (EU-only), but our auto-migration replaces with quantized v1.2-q across regions and mismatches enforcement checks.
- Risk: model variant semantics differ and invalidate residency matchers.
- Mitigation: Add explicit metadata on model artifacts for residency_compatibility boolean and supported_regions list; block cross-region substitution when strict residency enabled.

3) Third-party connectors with proxy rewrite
- Symptom: On-prem proxy rewrites Authorization header and removes X-Region hint.
- Risk: upstream enforcement cannot see original request context.
- Mitigation: recommend TLS mutual auth + signed region header (HMAC) between connector and gateway. Document connector changes in Solutions playbook.

4) Large-batch jobs spanning datasets in multiple regions
- Symptom: Batch ingestion references S3 objects in different regions and triggers enforcement.
- Mitigation: Surface per-object region and require customers to scope batch jobs to a single residency region or enable multi-region exception with audit trail.

5) Cache warmup-induced false-negatives
- Symptom: KV prefix cache warmed in US, later used for EU requests if routing not careful.
- Mitigation: Namespace caches by region and tenant. Add tags to cached entries with origin_region and TTL.

6) Cross-account inference pipelines (orchestration services)
- Symptom: Orchestrator takes outputs from EU tenant and feeds into US tenant pipeline.
- Mitigation: Provide pipeline-level residency checks and sticky partitioning; add pre-flight validation in orchestration layer.

Operational playbook snippets (quick actions)
- If advisory_violation_rate spikes > 1% in a cohort -> flip cohort back to advisory and open PD incident with customer-facing comms.
- If pilot customer reports degraded quality after region fallback -> capture sample payloads (redact PII) and run eval against pinned & fallback models, escalate to Applied ML.
- For persistent 403/residency_violation in canary -> create immediate rollback and notify customers in affected cohort within 1 hour.

Customer communication and opt-in model
- Draft email template (short): explain intent, risk profile, suggested migration steps, timeline, and contact info for migration support.
- Migration playbook: automated audit -> list mismatches -> suggested config changes -> run migration script -> validation tests.
- Offer extended migration assistance for enterprise customers (paid migration pack).

Metrics to track (per cohort):
- advisory_violation_count (int)
- softfail_to_hardfail_transition_count (events)
- customer_reported_sevs (count)
- cross_region_token_rate (pct of tokens served outside pinned region)
- median_latency_change_post-enforcement (ms)

Examples of Jira/PR actions to create now
- PD-430: implement X-Residency-Warning header and schema
- PD-431: cache namespacing by region
- PD-432: session-level residency token prototype
- github PR: infra/pull/1795 add per-request residency sampling

Open questions (to resolve before Phase 2)
- Do we need signed region headers for all Private connectors or just when proxying across trust boundaries?
- What SLA/legal language do we show for enforced hard-fail during migration windows? Legal to draft.
- Should soft-fail responses include an automated retry path to a fallback model (we need to assess billing implications)?

Checklist before flipping any cohort to hard-fail
- [ ] Observability dashboards for residency metrics published and shared
- [ ] Sample payload capture enabled and retention policy agreed
- [ ] Customer migration playbook published and tested with at least one solutions engagement
- [ ] Rollback runbook validated (time-to-rollback < 30 minutes)
- [ ] Communication templates (email + portal banner) approved by comms

Appendix: sample soft-fail response (proto)
- HTTP/1.1 200 OK
- X-Residency-Warning: 'true;target_region=eu-west-1;reason=session-handoff'
- Body: {
  "id": "gen-abc123",
  "text": "...",
  "meta": { "fallback": "gpt-lite-eu" }
}

Next steps (owners & dates)
- 2024-11-14: Enable advisory mode org-wide — Diego
- 2024-11-28: Choose 5 pilot customers and notify — Priya
- 2024-12-12: Implement X-Residency-Warning header (PD-430) — Platform
- 2025-01-08: Run first region cohort canary — Omar

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an operational-first draft. Look for missing edge cases in your customer accounts (Solutions), or missing infra constraints (SRE). Please add comments inline or ping me on #residency-rollout.
